question.text: Commodities futures contracts have which type of payoff profile?

answer.text: Linear payoff — profits and losses increase proportionally with price movement
Non-linear payoff — profits increase but losses are limited
Step payoff — profits jump at specific price levels
Exponential payoff — profits increase exponentially with price

explanation.text: The Logic: Commodity futures contracts have a linear payoff — for every unit change in the underlying price, the P&L changes by the same amount, with long gaining as price rises and short gaining as price falls. The source explicitly contrasts the linear payoff of futures with the non-linear payoff of options. The Trap: Non-linear with limited loss describes options, not futures. Step and exponential payoffs are not characteristic of commodity futures. Note: Because the payoff is linear and symmetric, equal-sized moves in the underlying generate equal-sized P&L for the buyer and the seller of the futures contract.
